specification.problem: Quantum state tomography of n qubits (dimension d=2^n) using a complete set of d+1 mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) that are generated cyclically by repeated application of a single unitary generator built from Hadamard and (controlled-)phase gates; the measured outcome statistics in all d+1 bases determine the density matrix.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scoped to (i) the general cyclic-MUB framework (unbiasedness condition, cyclic generator of order d+1, MUB-based tomographic inversion) and (ii) one tiny explicit instance: n=1 qubit (d=2), where a verifiable order-3 generator U = S H (phase gate times Hadamard) cycles the computational basis through the Y- and X-eigenbases, giving the complete set of 3 single-qubit MUBs. Out of scope: the paper's explicit multi-qubit (two-, three-, four-qubit) generators built from Hadamard and controlled-phase gates, the classification of entanglement structures of the resulting MUB sets, and the circuits implementing the various entanglement classes; none of these are specified in the abstract and are not invented here.

symbols.meaning: computational-basis state, j encoded as an n-bit string (little-endian: qubit 0 is the least significant bit when n>1)
cyclic MUB generator, a unitary with U^{d+1} proportional to the identity
k-th basis of the MUB set, \mathcal{B}_k=\{U^k|j\rangle\}_j
rank-one projector onto the j-th vector of basis \mathcal{B}_k
probability of outcome j when the state is measured in basis \mathcal{B}_k
unknown n-qubit density matrix to be reconstructed
symbols.domain: positive semidefinite, trace one, d\times d

symbols.meaning: controlled-phase (controlled-Z) gate between qubits a and b, diag(1,1,1,-1)

equations.label: Mutual unbiasedness condition
equations.description: Two orthonormal bases are mutually unbiased when every overlap between a vector of one and a vector of the other has squared modulus exactly 1/d; a complete set for d=2^n contains d+1 such bases.
equations.justification: Standard definition of mutually unbiased bases; existence of d+1 MUBs in prime-power dimension is established background.
assumptions: d is a prime power (true for qubits, d=2^n)

equations.label: Cyclic generation of the MUB set
equations.description: All d+1 bases are obtained by repeatedly applying one generator U to the computational basis; U has order d+1 up to a global phase, so the sequence of bases is cyclic. This is an exact (not approximate) relation; the bases are required to satisfy eq_1.
equations.abstract_quote: cyclic generation of mutually unbiased bases
equations.justification: The abstract states the method is based on cyclic generation of MUBs; the natural mathematical content of 'cyclic' is a single unitary whose powers produce all bases and which returns to the identity (up to phase) after d+1 steps. The specific choice of U in the paper is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: 'Cyclic' is interpreted as a single generator of order d+1 modulo global phase acting on the computational basis

equations.label: Structure of the basic generator (Hadamard and controlled-phase gates)
equations.latex: U = H^{\otimes n}\, D, \qquad D = \prod_{(a,b)\in E} CZ_{ab}\;\prod_{c\in V} P_c, \quad P_c\in\{\mathbb{1}, S\}
equations.description: Proposed form of the generator: a layer of Hadamards preceded by a diagonal network D of controlled-phase gates (edge set E) and possibly single-qubit phase gates (vertex set V). The abstract only states which gate types are needed; the precise sets E, V and the gate ordering that make U satisfy eq_1 and eq_2 for n=2,3,4 are NOT determined here.
equations.abstract_quote: The basic generator requires only Hadamard and controlled-phase gates
equations.justification: Inferred from the stated gate set; since controlled-phase gates are diagonal and Hadamards are the only non-diagonal element, the generator decomposes as Hadamards times a diagonal phase network. The explicit pattern is missing information, so this equation is a structural template, not a verified construction.
assumptions: Generator consists of a single Hadamard layer times a diagonal gate; multiple alternating layers are possible in the actual paper
Single-qubit phase gates may or may not be part of the paper's construction

equations.label: Explicit one-qubit instance (n=1, d=2)
equations.description: Smallest explicit instance: Hadamard followed by the phase gate S=diag(1,i) is a cyclic generator of order 3 (up to global phase e^{i\pi/4}) that maps the Z-eigenbasis to the Y-eigenbasis to the X-eigenbasis, which form the complete set of 3 single-qubit MUBs (all cross overlaps have squared modulus exactly 1/2). Uses a single-qubit phase gate rather than a controlled-phase gate because no two-qubit gate exists for n=1.
equations.justification: Chosen as the smallest verifiable instance of eqs. 1-2; direct matrix multiplication gives (SH)^3 = ((1+i)/\sqrt{2})\,\mathbb{1} and the three bases are the standard Pauli eigenbases, which are mutually unbiased. This is not claimed to be the paper's generator.
assumptions: Instance chosen by the reconstruction, not taken from the abstract
Gate ordering: H applied first, then S

equations.label: Outcome probabilities in basis k
equations.description: Measuring in basis \mathcal{B}_k is implemented by applying (U^\dagger)^k to the state and then measuring in the computational basis; outcome j occurs with probability p_{k,j}. In practice p_{k,j} is estimated from finite shot counts, so the estimated value approximates the exact probability.
equations.justification: Born rule and the standard equivalence between measuring in a rotated basis and un-rotating the state before a computational-basis measurement.
assumptions: Projective (ideal) measurements; finite-sample estimates replace exact probabilities

equations.label: MUB tomographic reconstruction
equations.description: For a complete set of d+1 MUBs the d(d+1) projectors form an informationally complete set and the density matrix is recovered exactly (as a linear inversion) from the outcome probabilities; with estimated probabilities the result is an estimate and may require a positivity-restoring post-processing step.
equations.justification: Standard MUB state-reconstruction formula following from \sum_j \Pi_{k,j}=\mathbb{1} and the unbiasedness condition eq_1.
assumptions: Exact probabilities; with finite statistics this is a linear-inversion estimator

registers.name: data
registers.role: holds the unknown n-qubit state \rho to be reconstructed; for n>1 qubit 0 is the least significant bit of j in |j\rangle

specification.initial_state: Unknown state \rho on the data register, prepared identically for every repetition (for the n=1 instance, an arbitrary single-qubit density matrix).

steps.description: Fix n and d=2^n; choose a cyclic MUB generator U satisfying eq_2 and producing bases satisfying eq_1 (for the n=1 instance take U_1 = S H from eq_4; for n>1 the generator has the Hadamard/controlled-phase form eq_3 whose explicit pattern is not provided by the abstract).
For each k = 0, 1, ..., d: prepare \rho on the data register and apply the circuit (U^\dagger)^k, i.e. k repetitions of the inverse generator (for n=1: k applications of H S^\dagger).
Measure all n qubits in the computational basis, record outcome j; repeat many shots per k to estimate p_{k,j}.
Combine the estimated probabilities over all d+1 bases to reconstruct \rho via linear inversion.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis projective measurement of all n data qubits after applying (U^\dagger)^k, for each k = 0,...,d; equivalent to measuring directly in basis \mathcal{B}_k. Total of d+1 measurement settings (3 for the n=1 instance).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate p_{k,j} from outcome frequencies for each k and j; compute \rho via eq_6; optionally project onto the set of physical (positive semidefinite, unit-trace) states to correct finite-sample errors.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied, so the reconstruction chose the smallest useful instance: a single qubit (d=2) with the order-3 generator U_1 = S H, verified by direct matrix multiplication; this instance is a choice of this reconstruction and is not stated in the abstract
Cyclic generation is interpreted as a single unitary U of order d+1 (modulo global phase) acting on the computational basis
The multi-qubit generator is assumed to decompose as a Hadamard layer times a diagonal controlled-phase network (eq_3); its exact structure is unknown
Ideal gates and projective measurements; finite shot statistics make the reconstruction approximate
Little-endian integer encoding of computational-basis labels when n>1
missing_information: Explicit n-qubit cyclic generator (which qubits receive Hadamards, which pairs receive controlled-phase gates, gate ordering and number of layers) for n = 2, 3, 4
Definition and classification of the 'different entanglement structures' of the MUB sets and how the generator is modified to realize each class
The quantum circuits implementing the various entanglement classes analyzed in the paper
Any discussion of the global phase \varphi and of generators of order d+1 in the Clifford group that the paper may rely on
Whether the paper's tomographic inversion uses the standard linear MUB formula (eq_6) or a different estimator
